main_point: GitHub removed the open-source video downloader youtube-dl following a DMCA notice from the RIAA, a move criticized by digital rights advocates as an overreaction that ignores the tool's legitimate uses for public domain content and fair use, prompting users to bypass the ban by hosting the code elsewhere.

aliases: a video-sharing platform for citizen journalism
one of the maintainers of youtube-dl script
the founder of the Free Software Foundation

statements.text: The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) issued a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) takedown notice to the code hosting platform GitHub, asserting that the open-source video downloader youtube-dl was specifically engineered to bypass the technological protections employed by authorized streaming services and to distribute copyrighted music without permission. This legal action, which stripped identifying metadata before publication, relies on the software's internal unit tests as evidence of intent, despite the tool's primary design for downloading public domain content and Creative Commons licensed material.
statements.text_short: The RIAA sent a DMCA notice to GitHub claiming the open-source video downloader was designed to bypass streaming protections.

statements.text: The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) points to specific comments within the source code of the open-source video downloader youtube-dl as proof that the software was created with the intent to circumvent the technological measures protecting content on YouTube. This argument forms the core of the RIAA's legal challenge, which seeks to have the tool and its associated code repositories removed from the GitHub platform, even though the software also functions to download legally available public domain and Creative Commons works.
statements.text_short: The RIAA cites code comments in the open-source video downloader as evidence of intent to circumvent YouTube's protections.

statements.text: The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) is alleging a violation of 17 U.S. Code § 1201, which prohibits the circumvention of technological measures that effectively control access to copyrighted works. This legal framework is being used to justify a demand that the code hosting platform GitHub make the open-source video downloader youtube-dl and its various derivative versions inaccessible, arguing that the software's ability to bypass digital locks infringes upon federal anti-circumvention laws regardless of how the tool is actually used.
statements.text_short: The RIAA alleges a violation of U.S. anti-circumvention law to demand that GitHub block the open-source video downloader.

statements.text: The Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) has requested that the code hosting platform GitHub make inaccessible a specific list of forked versions of the open-source video downloader youtube-dl. This broad takedown request targets derivative projects that the RIAA believes are related to the original tool, aiming to ensure that no accessible version of the software remains available on the platform, even if those specific forks do not contain the same code comments cited as evidence of copyright infringement.
statements.text_short: The RIAA requested that GitHub block multiple forked versions of the open-source video downloader.

statements.text: When copyright holders voluntarily release their work under a Creative Commons Attribution license, they explicitly grant the public the right to freely own, share, and modify that content, provided users properly attribute the original author. This legal framework ensures that legitimate uses of such material remain accessible to everyone, regardless of the restrictions imposed by other entities on the platforms hosting the content.
statements.text_short: Creative Commons licenses grant the public broad rights to share and modify voluntarily released works.

statements.text: The open-source tool youtube-dl is designed to support fair use and evidence gathering, demonstrating that the tool's functionality extends beyond copyright infringement. Furthermore, standard web browsers can already download and record copyrighted photos and videos, proving that no technological barriers effectively prevent users from accessing and sharing digital content.
statements.text_short: youtube-dl supports fair use, and standard browsers can already download copyrighted content.

statements.text: The decision by the software hosting platform GitHub to remove the youtube-dl tool backfired, triggering a 'Streisand effect' where the ban inadvertently caused the software's source code to spread more widely. Users successfully bypassed the restriction by sharing the code through decentralized networks, self-hosted servers, and the Tor network, rendering the removal effort counterproductive.
statements.text_short: GitHub's removal of the tool backfired, causing users to share the code via alternative channels.

statements.text: Following the removal of the tool, users of the software hosting platform engaged in acts of digital vandalism to restore access, with one individual merging the source code into the very repository designated for copyright takedown notices. This strategic move allowed users to access the code directly from the DMCA folder, provided they knew the specific commit identifier, effectively circumventing the intended ban.
statements.text_short: Users vandalized the repository to merge the code into the DMCA folder, restoring access.

actor_aliases: the founder of the Free Software Foundation
statements.text: Richard Stallman, the founder of the Free Software Foundation, has long maintained that digital rights management systems are fundamentally flawed and harmful to software freedom, a stance that informs his sharp criticism of the RIAA's demand to remove the open-source video downloader from GitHub.
statements.text_short: Richard Stallman condemns digital rights management as inherently harmful to software freedom.

actor_aliases: one of the maintainers of youtube-dl script
statements.text: The maintainer of the open-source video downloader could restore the project's code on GitHub by the weekend, yet views the RIAA's demand for the tool's complete removal as an unacceptable and damaging outcome that undermines the software's utility.
statements.text_short: The youtube-dl maintainer can restore the code but deems the RIAA's removal demand unacceptable.

actor_aliases: one of the maintainers of youtube-dl script
statements.text: The project maintainers cannot promise they will fully comply with the RIAA's demands to remove the video downloader, noting that they must balance the risk of legal retaliation against the need to preserve the tool for users who rely on it for lawful purposes.
statements.text_short: The project maintainers will likely resist the RIAA's demands to protect the tool's availability.

statements.text: While the Electronic Frontier Foundation has not yet issued a formal response to inquiries regarding the takedown, the news organization has already contacted the project's former maintainers to gather details on the situation and the community's reaction to the RIAA's actions.
statements.text_short: The EFF has not yet commented, but journalists are actively seeking information from the project team.

statements.text: While the tool in question is designed to download content from over 1,000 services, it cannot access videos protected by Digital Rights Management technology, such as those found on YouTube Movies, because the platform enforces these restrictions to prevent unauthorized copying.
statements.text_short: DRM protection on specific YouTube content prevents the open-source downloader from accessing those files.

statements.text: The open-source video downloader allows users to play high-quality videos on hardware devices like Raspberry Pis that are otherwise unable to access the streaming services due to technical limitations or lack of native support.
statements.text_short: The tool enables video playback on devices that cannot natively access certain streaming services.

statements.text: Although the inclusion of copyrighted test cases in the source code was driven by user demand for specific video support, these elements can be easily removed to resolve legal concerns without compromising the tool's overall functionality or its legitimate uses for public domain material.
statements.text_short: User-requested copyrighted test cases can be removed from the tool's codebase without affecting its core functions.
